title: rosa canina subsp. crataegina
intro: Rosa canina subsp. crataegina, commonly known as the wild rose or Scotch rose, is a subspecies of the Rosa canina species. This plant has been valued for its potential health benefits, including its ability to support digestive health, reduce inflammation, and provide antioxidant properties. Rosa canina subsp. crataegina is reported to exhibit therapeutic actions such as anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial activities, which may be attributed to its bioactive constituents, including flavonoids, phenolic acids, and essential oils. The bioactive constituents of Rosa canina subsp. crataegina may also include triterpenoids, carotenoids, and other compounds that contribute to its therapeutic properties.
